newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain to improve Madrid airport after fire.
newsitem.headline: Spain to improve Madrid airport after fire.

text.p: Tuesday night's total shutdown of Madrid's Barajas airport should never be repeated, the Spanish airport authority's chairman said on Wednesday, announcing a series of measures to improve safety and ease overcrowding.
A fire closed the airport for five hours, forcing airlines to delay or cancel almost 300 flights.

"It's inconceivable that the infrastructure of an airport as important as Barajas is insufficient to cope with any emergency and that we had to close the airport in order to put out a fire and restore the electricity supply," AENA chairman Fernando Pina told a news conference.
"We have put in place a shock plan from today...so that this situation can never be repeated," he added.

Pina declined to comment on reports that workmen, whose drill ruptured electrical cables and started a fire in a service gallery on Tuesday morning, had been working without clearance or plans of the airport. He said an investigation was underway.
Flag carrier Iberia said the closure affected 95 of its own flights and 15,000 passengers. It had to put 200 people up in hotels overnight and transport hundreds of others to railway stations.
The fire was supposedly extinguished by midday, but it later broke out again and the airport had to be closed as night fell because there were no runway lights.

AENA will now revise and improve all safety procedures and is preparing a former U.S. military base at nearby Torrejon to take some of Barajas's commercial flights and relieve congestion at the capital's main airport.
Torrejon could take passengers, who will have been previously checked in at Barajas, as early as next week, added Pina who took over as AENA chairman only this summer.
Independent Spanish airlines, who compete with flag carrier Iberia, have said they are willing to shift their flights to Torrejon.

The government is also studying the possibility of using the smaller Getafe airport west of the city as an alternative to Barajas which is operating at or beyond saturation levels and will not have a third runway before the end of 1998.
